subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Metastatic hormone receptor positive breast cancer: targeted and endocrine options

steps.tx: In **hormone receptor positive** metastatic disease, the usual first line approach pairs an **endocrine agent** with a **CDK4/6 inhibitor** such as palbociclib, unless the patient has life threatening visceral involvement needing faster control. The endocrine partner is selected according to menopausal state and previous treatment. Premenopausal women also need **ovarian function suppression** so that the endocrine drug acts effectively.

rows: Postmenopausal, or premenopausal with ovarian suppression

steps.tx: **Fulvestrant** is a **selective estrogen receptor degrader**, acting as a pure antagonist with no agonist activity. It binds the receptor and marks it for breakdown, lowering nuclear ER alpha levels. The standard dose is 500 mg by intramuscular injection on days 1, 15 and 29, then monthly. Injection site pain and hot flushes are common, and platelet counts matter because the injection is intramuscular.

steps.tx: **CDK4 and CDK6 inhibitors** added to endocrine therapy improve progression free survival in first line disease. **Palbociclib** is given at 125 mg daily for three weeks, then one week off. Other agents in this class follow their own schedules, so check the product information. **Neutropenia** is the main limiting toxicity, so counts are monitored and doses are held or reduced when needed. Diarrhoea and fatigue also occur.

rows: 125 mg daily, 3 weeks on, 1 week off

steps.tx: Resistance to endocrine therapy often arises through **ESR1 mutations**, which can be detected on **circulating tumour DNA**. After endocrine and CDK4/6 failure, an **oral SERD** is an option for ESR1 mutated disease. **PI3K pathway** alterations can be targeted by a **PI3K inhibitor** given with fulvestrant. **Capivasertib** with fulvestrant covers PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations. Both PI3K and AKT drugs cause **hyperglycaemia**, so glucose is monitored.
